docs.syntax: =MAX(0,reorder_at-on_hand) floors a shortfall at zero; MAX(0,a-b) over totals nets it out
docs.explain:
MAX returns the largest number it is given, so MAX(0,C2-B2) reports a shortfall and never a negative. Where the reorder point sits above stock, the subtraction stands. Where stock is higher, the zero wins. The bolt row has ten to reorder against four on hand, so it asks for six.

The second screen asks the same question of the whole sheet: the reorder column comes to 39, the stock column to 27, and the net shortfall is 12. MAX holds that at zero in a month when the warehouse is ahead. The nut's surplus cancels part of the washer's gap, which is why flooring the rows one by one would add to 16.

The guard matters because the column has to fill down. Copy C2-B2 into four rows without it and the nut asks for minus four, which no purchase order can carry. With the zero in place the same fill gives figures you can add straight into the order.

errors.text: A cell in the subtraction holds text, which is not a number to work with.
MAX is misspelled in the call, and Excel returns #NAME?.
MAX is left off, so an over-stocked row asks for a negative number of parts.

docs.atWork: Turning on-hand stock and reorder points into an order quantity that never goes negative.
docs.outcome: Floor a row's shortfall at zero, then net the whole sheet the same way.
docs.teaches: MAX as a zero floor, over one row and then over two column totals
docs.dataset: Four parts with stock, reorder points and one answer cell

screens.prompt: In D2, report how many bolts to order, never a negative number.

hints.syntax: =MAX(0,C2-B2): the shortfall, with zero as the floor.
hints.func-max: The order quantity has to stop at zero on an over-stocked row.
hints.require-ref: Stock on hand is in B2 and the reorder point is in C2.
hints.value: Ten to reorder less four in stock leaves six.
hints.error: A text cell in the subtraction gives #VALUE! instead of an order quantity.

reject.why: an over-stocked row would ask for a negative order
stock minus the reorder point is negative for a short part
one spare bolt is not what the reorder point asks for
two spare parts are added to every row
the formula reads the second part rather than B2
the order quantity is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, add up how far the sheet falls short of every reorder point.

hints.syntax: =MAX(0,SUM(C2:C5)-SUM(B2:B5)): two column totals, floored at zero.
hints.func-max: The sheet can be ahead of its reorder points, so the net needs a floor.
hints.func-sum: Both sides of the subtraction are column totals.
hints.value: 39 to reorder against 27 in stock leaves 12.
hints.error: The grader says the formula stops with an error, and a division by zero is the usual cause.

reject.why: nothing keeps the net shortfall at zero on a well-stocked sheet
the subtraction is the wrong way round, so the floor swallows it
the last part is missing from the stock total
the last part is missing from the reorder total
the first part's stock is missing from the total
one part's shortfall is not the whole sheet's
the shortfall is then divided by zero
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

seo.title: A reorder report with no negative stock
seo.description: MAX wrapped around reorder point minus on hand does nothing where stock is short and floors the rest at zero, so the column reads as an order quantity.
